page: Vultr voc-m-2c-16gb-200s-amd is an instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute family, featuring an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC processor. The server is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. It includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is provided via a bundled 200 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes a single complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU test places this instance in the top tier (top 10%) with a score of 3135.07, whereas multi-core performance falls into the average category at 6221.86. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is average, measuring 73.36 GB/sec for read-only and 52.37 GB/sec for write operations, though small-block cached read bandwidth is relatively weak at 299.56 GB/sec. Passmark CPU tests consistently rank in the bottom 25%, reflecting limitations in extended instructions, encryption, and physics calculations.

This hardware profile presents specific performance tradeoffs. Database operations are a notable bottleneck, with Passmark database operations scoring in the bottom 10% and Redis SET operations performing in the bottom 25% at 4.84 million operations per second. Static web serving throughput is also low at 2.14 GB/sec. However, the instance handles lightweight text generation reasonably well, achieving an average 112.37 tokens/sec on a 135M LLM model, though it struggles with larger models. Given the generous 16 GB memory allocation relative to its 2 vCPUs, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive parallel processing, such as caching layers, lightweight application servers, or memory-heavy development environments.
description: Vultr voc-m-2c-16gb-200s-amd is an AMD EPYC-powered instance from the Optimized Cloud Compute family, featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs, 16.0 GB of RAM, and a 200 GB NVMe SSD. Operating on an x86_64 architecture at 2.0 GHz, it offers a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Performance benchmarks show a strong single-core stress-ng result in the top 10%, contrasted by average multi-core and weak Passmark CPU scores. Memory bandwidth is average for large blocks but weak for cached small blocks. Significant performance bottlenecks exist in database operations and static web serving, both scoring in the bottom 10%. Consequently, this server is best suited for memory-intensive but compute-light applications, such as caching, staging environments, or lightweight memory-bound services, rather than high-throughput databases or intensive web serving.
